cover letter
Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training

The Practicum Education & Specialized Training Coordinator works under the direction of the Senior Director of Admissions, Advising, and Student Experience and collaboratively with the Dean's Office to manage program resources and conduct analytical studies of moderate scope and complexity to address policy and procedural issues. This position maintains secure systems for collecting student health clearances, student placement data, and other programmatic data, while coordinating administration of the Pupil Personnel Services Credential (PPSC) in Social Work and workforce programs.
Data and Systems Maintenance

The Practicum Education & Specialized Training Coordinator supports practicum education by managing business partnerships with internship sites, coordinating the online interface for student internship search and matching, and managing learning contracts and student evaluations. This role handles sensitive onboarding data, including Protected Health Information (PHI) and background checks. Additionally, the position manages university-sponsored training and events and ensures data management and quality assurance in accordance with program policy.
Applies professional concepts to perform maintenance and analysis of data and systems pertaining to moderately complex projects, policies, and/or processes and functions.

Supports practicum education operations by maintaining accurate, confidential, secure, and timely data within multiple data management systems. With guidance from the Associate Dean for Curriculum and the Senior Director of Admissions, Advising, and Student Experience, ensures consistency and quality assurance in accordance with the national accrediting body, the Council on Social Work Education, when engaging with and maintaining policies, projects, and issues that support program operations.

Provides regular technical support and training for database issues encountered by students, agency partners, and/or school representatives. Resolves procedural and technical issues in the context of department policies and procedures with a customer-service mindset.

Ensures proper database permissions and access for practicum instructors, faculty, students, advisors, and administrators, and that security roles and data storage align with UC data protection requirements.
Proactively identifies, proposes, and executes approved business process improvement projects, taking into account business practice and technical considerations.
Helps establish standards, guidelines, and best practices for database deliverables and program processes.
Ensures that operations and digital content comply with local and federal policies.

Gathers and assembles analytical and factual data on assigned problems and issues to prepare reports and/or analyses summarizing information on the assigned issues and commenting on other significance for internal department constituents.
Prepares student placement, agency contact, student competency, and other reports as requested. In collaboration with the team, identifies trends, forecasts needs, and supports further analysis.
Performs analytical studies on a variety of policies, research initiatives, programs, and issues.
Provides recommendations and guidelines involving program initiatives.
Document and Contract Management
Prepares, edits, modifies, and/or distributes documents, including research reports, manuscripts, presentations, proposals, and contracts.

Manages the School's affiliation agreements with multiple practicum agencies: tracks agreement expiration dates, communicates with agency contacts and UC Berkeley's Business Contracts Office staff, and identifies and escalates risks to the Dean's Office.
Negotiates affiliation agreements with partner agencies that clearly outline the respective degrees of liability for UCB and the agency, consistent with UC Berkeley's risk management objectives.
Coordinates the renewal process for the School of Social Welfare's general and professional liability insurance policies.
Stakeholder and Event Support
Provides a variety of efficient support for both internal and external stakeholders in their unit to achieve smooth operation of practicum education, including:

Serves as the first point of email, and /or in-person contact for students, faculty, staff, and the public regarding social work/welfare practicum education and available specialized training programs (e.g., Child Welfare Scholars, Pupil Personnel Services Credential, and others that may arise).

Coordinates logistical aspects of the placement process for practica, which includes, but is not limited to, collaborating with admissions staff, distributing student and agency forms and communications; maintaining statuses of student placements; attending meetings and consulting with the Practicum Team to secure student placements; and maintaining timely correspondence with all relevant parties.

Coordinates logistical aspects of and provides live support for practicum and specialized training program-related events (e.g., Practicum Instructor Training, Skills Workshops, Placement Process Events, and Fairs). This includes, but is not limited to, working with relevant staff to secure appropriate venues (including in-person and online events), refreshments, and supplies; coordinating and communicating with event participants before, during, and after the event; and collaborating with other Dean's Office staff and faculty to ensure event goals are met.

Coordinates logistical aspects of student selection/application processes for specialized training programs (e.g., Child Welfare Scholars, Pupil Personnel Services Credential). This includes the distribution and collection of student service agreements and other required documentation for instructional grant programs. Coordinates the collection of student default payments and communications related to students entering repayment programs and alerts the Dean's Office financial roles. Participates in instructional grant team/funder/stipend program calls and meetings as needed, and other tasks as necessary to support instructional grant program administration.
Career and Professional Development
Provides a variety of administrative duties in support of identifying appropriate student matches for instructional grant/stipend programs and career and professional development programming.

Collaborates with Practicum Education and other Dean's Office staff and relevant on-and off-campus resources and centers to provide administrative support in the planning and implementation of career development programming, expanding opportunities for skill-building, mentorship, research, and experiential learning.
Collaborates on assessments of learning, continuing education, and professional development needs of current students and the social work practice community.
Other duties as assigned.
Able to travel up to 5% of the time and work occasional evenings/weekends for special events.

Knowledge of and/or can quickly learn computer application programs, major office, database, and internet software packages, such as proficiency with Google Suite (email, calendar, docs, sheets, forms, etc.) and Microsoft Office Suite, especially Word and Excel, and relational databases.
Working knowledge of applicable policy analysis techniques.

Excellent communication, service orientation, interpersonal and problem-solving skills, attention to detail, with demonstrated active listening skills and an ability to communicate effectively with all levels of staff, both verbally and in writing.
Absolute ability to maintain strict confidentiality per the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA) regulations.

Skills in judgment and decision-making, problem-solving, identifying measures of system/process performance, and the actions to improve performance through application/process configuration and programming/organizational techniques.
Demonstrates ability to analyze, research, and synthesize large amounts of data with strong attention to detail.
Solid ability to use organizational skills to multitask in a high-volume environment and adapt to changing priorities.

Demonstrated interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively across the organization at all levels; high degree of emotional intelligence; political acumen; ability to build consensus among diverse populations, including faculty, staff, and students.
Absolute reliability to manage projects and meet and communicate about deadlines.

Knowledge of and/or can quickly learn and implement university/higher education and departmental rules and regulations, processes, especially as it relates to risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences.

pay.source_text: ience. The budgeted hourly range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $31.68 - $43.09. This is a non-exempt, bi-weekly paid position. This is a full-time (40 hours/week) Career position
